clinical_note: Blood group or antigen-antibody reactions detected by agglutination help in identifying infections, blood typing, and immune responses. Results should be interpreted along with clinical findings.
Albert staining is used for identification of specific bacteria such as Corynebacterium diphtheriae. Presence of characteristic staining patterns helps in diagnosis of infectious diseases.
Anaerobic culture is performed to detect bacteria that grow in oxygen-free environments. It is useful in diagnosing deep tissue and abscess infections caused by anaerobic organisms.
Aspiration samples are collected from body fluids or lesions to detect infection, inflammation, or malignancy. Results should be correlated with clinical and imaging findings.
Autoanalyzer-based tests provide precise biochemical measurements for various parameters. Results depend on calibration, reagent quality, and patient condition.
Automated culture systems improve detection and identification of microorganisms with higher accuracy and faster turnaround time. Useful in diagnosing bloodstream and systemic infections.
Analysis of body fluids helps in diagnosing infections, inflammatory conditions, and malignancies. Results should be interpreted along with clinical findings and other laboratory investigations.
Benedict test is used to detect the presence of reducing sugars in urine, which may indicate conditions like diabetes mellitus or renal disorders.
Biochemical tests evaluate organ function, metabolic status, and electrolyte balance. Results should be correlated with clinical condition and other investigations.
Complete blood count assesses red cells, white cells, and platelets, helping diagnose anemia, infections, inflammation, and hematological disorders.
Coagulation tests evaluate the blood clotting mechanism and help diagnose bleeding disorders, thrombotic conditions, and monitor anticoagulant therapy.
Concentration techniques are used to increase detection of parasites or microorganisms in samples, improving diagnostic accuracy in infections.
Culture and sensitivity tests identify infectious organisms and determine appropriate antibiotics, guiding effective treatment.
Culture tests are performed to detect and identify microorganisms causing infections. Results help in diagnosis and treatment planning.
Chemiluminescence immunoassay (CLIA) is a sensitive method used for detecting hormones, proteins, and other analytes with high accuracy.
Clotting assays assess the functionality of clotting factors and help diagnose coagulation disorders and monitor therapy.
Cardiac markers are used to evaluate heart muscle injury and aid in diagnosis and management of cardiac conditions such as myocardial infarction.
Colorimetric methods measure the concentration of substances based on color intensity and are commonly used in biochemical analysis.
Dipstick tests provide rapid screening of urine for parameters such as glucose, protein, ketones, and infections. Results are preliminary and should be confirmed with further testing if required.
Enzyme Immunoassay (EIA) is used to detect antigens or antibodies in the sample and is commonly applied in infectious disease and hormone testing.
Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA) is a sensitive technique used for detecting antibodies, antigens, and proteins in various diseases including infections and autoimmune disorders.
Endocrinology tests evaluate hormone levels and help diagnose disorders related to thyroid, adrenal, pituitary, and other endocrine glands.
Electrophoresis separates proteins or other molecules based on their charge and size, aiding in diagnosis of disorders such as multiple myeloma and hemoglobinopathies.
Fungal culture is performed to detect and identify fungal infections. It is useful in diagnosing superficial and systemic mycoses.
Functional assays assess the activity or function of specific biological components, helping evaluate physiological or pathological conditions.
Functional tests evaluate the performance of organs or systems, assisting in diagnosis and monitoring of various diseases.
Fluorometric methods measure substances based on fluorescence intensity and are used in sensitive biochemical and immunological assays.
Flow cytometry analyzes cells based on size, structure, and markers, and is widely used in hematology, immunology, and cancer diagnosis.
Guaiac test is used to detect occult blood in stool, which may indicate gastrointestinal bleeding or related conditions.
Gram staining is a fundamental technique used to classify bacteria into gram-positive and gram-negative groups, aiding in early diagnosis of infections.
Histopathological examination involves microscopic study of tissues to diagnose diseases such as cancer, infections, and inflammatory conditions.
Hemoglobin studies help identify variants and abnormalities such as thalassemia and sickle cell disease, aiding in diagnosis of hematological disorders.
Hematology tests evaluate blood components including red cells, white cells, and platelets, helping diagnose anemia, infections, and blood disorders.
Hemolysis tests assess the breakdown of red blood cells and help diagnose hemolytic anemias and related conditions.
Hemagglutination tests detect antigen-antibody reactions involving red blood cells and are used in blood grouping and certain infectious disease testing.
High Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC) is used to separate and quantify compounds, commonly applied in hemoglobin analysis and metabolic studies.
Hormone tests measure levels of various hormones to evaluate endocrine function and diagnose hormonal imbalances.
Immunohematology involves testing of blood groups, compatibility, and antibody detection, important for transfusion medicine.
Immunoassays detect specific antigens or antibodies and are widely used in diagnosis of infections, hormonal disorders, and autoimmune diseases.
India ink staining is used to detect encapsulated organisms such as Cryptococcus species in clinical samples.
Indirect Fluorescent Antibody (IFA) test is used to detect antibodies against specific pathogens and is useful in diagnosing infectious and autoimmune diseases.
Immunology tests evaluate the immune system and help diagnose infections, autoimmune disorders, and immunodeficiency conditions.
Immunofluorescence techniques use fluorescent labels to detect specific antigens or antibodies in tissues or cells.
Interferon Gamma Release Assay (IGRA) is used to detect latent or active tuberculosis infection by measuring immune response to TB antigens.
KOH mount is used for rapid detection of fungal elements in clinical samples by dissolving keratin and clearing background material.
Lowenstein-Jensen culture is used for isolation of Mycobacterium species, particularly in diagnosis of tuberculosis.
Liquid Based Cytology (LBC) is used for examination of cells, especially in cervical screening, to detect precancerous and cancerous changes.
Liquid Chromatography�Tandem Mass Spectrometry (LC-MS/MS) is a highly sensitive technique used for precise quantification of drugs, hormones, and metabolites.
Microscopic examination helps detect cells, microorganisms, and other elements in samples, aiding in diagnosis of infections and pathological conditions.
Mycobacteria Growth Indicator Tube (MGIT) culture is used for rapid detection of mycobacterial infections including tuberculosis.
Line Probe Assay (LPA) is a molecular method used for detection of genetic mutations associated with drug resistance in infections such as tuberculosis.
Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) is used to detect genetic material of pathogens with high sensitivity and specificity for early diagnosis of infections.
Microbiological tests identify infectious organisms such as bacteria, viruses, fungi, and parasites, guiding diagnosis and treatment.
Physical examination of samples assesses characteristics such as color, clarity, and consistency, providing preliminary diagnostic information.
CBNAAT is a cartridge-based PCR test used for rapid detection of tuberculosis and rifampicin resistance.
Panel tests involve a group of related tests performed together to assess specific conditions or organ systems comprehensively.
Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) detects genetic material of pathogens and is widely used for diagnosis of infectious diseases.
Rapid immunoassays provide quick detection of antigens or antibodies, useful for screening and early diagnosis of infections.
Rapid tests offer quick preliminary results for various conditions, but may require confirmation with standard laboratory methods.
Solubility tests are used to differentiate hemoglobin variants, particularly in screening for conditions like sickle cell disease.
Semen analysis evaluates male fertility by assessing sperm count, motility, morphology, and other parameters.
Stool examination helps detect infections, parasites, digestive disorders, and gastrointestinal bleeding.
Staining techniques enhance visualization of cells and microorganisms, aiding in identification and diagnosis of infections and diseases.
Sterility testing is performed to ensure absence of viable microorganisms in samples, especially in pharmaceutical and clinical products.
Special stains are used to identify specific cellular components or microorganisms not visible with routine staining methods.
Serological tests detect antibodies or antigens in blood, helping diagnose infections, autoimmune diseases, and immune status.
Spectroscopy measures the interaction of light with substances to determine concentration and composition in biochemical analysis.
Tube method is a laboratory technique used in various tests including blood grouping and compatibility testing.
Toxicology tests detect and measure toxic substances, drugs, or poisons in the body, aiding in diagnosis and management of poisoning.
Tumor markers are substances produced by cancer cells or the body in response to cancer, used for diagnosis, monitoring, and prognosis.
Therapeutic drug monitoring measures drug levels in the body to ensure effective dosage and avoid toxicity.
Urine analysis helps evaluate kidney function, metabolic disorders, and detect infections or systemic diseases.
Visual examination assesses physical characteristics of samples such as color and clarity, providing initial diagnostic clues.
Western blot is used to detect specific proteins and is commonly used as a confirmatory test in infectious and autoimmune diseases.
Ziehl-Neelsen staining is used to detect acid-fast bacilli, particularly Mycobacterium species causing tuberculosis.
Ziehl-Neelsen staining identifies acid-fast organisms and is essential in diagnosis of tuberculosis and related infections.
Modified Ziehl-Neelsen stain is used for detection of partially acid-fast organisms such as certain parasites and bacteria.
